_comment: Editor default demo scene (step E2, docs/06-editor-roadmap.md) -- opened automatically when no scene path is given on the command line. The Editor's own Scene View doesn't wire a physics callback (read-only load, see engine::scene::LoadScene's own comment), so the "collider"+"rigidbody" pair below spawns cleanly with the ECS components present but no live Jolt body -- it only actually simulates in Play Mode (editor_play, which does wire PhysicsWorld). "isStatic": false here is deliberately not the RigidbodyComponent default (true) -- proves RigidbodyComponent::isStatic (post-Editor-E8) actually round-trips through a Save now, a gap ExtractEntityDescs() used to silently drop a whole "rigidbody" block over (see SceneDocument.h's own comment) -- watch this entity fall under gravity in Play Mode, then Save from the Editor's Scene View and confirm the reloaded file still has "isStatic": false, not vanished or silently reset to the default. "guid" below is assets/m1_cube.glb's actual, committed Asset GUID (see assets/m1_cube.glb.meta). The middle cube's "scripts" array only does anything in Play Mode (editor/play_main.cpp) -- the Editor's own read-only Scene View has no AttachScriptFn wired up, so it just sits there like any other entity when merely viewing/editing this scene. The last entity's "parent": 2 (post-Editor-E8 hierarchy, docs/07-unity-parity-analysis.md) makes it a child of the RotateScript cube -- its own position [1.5,0,0] is local to that parent, so in Play Mode it visibly orbits as the parent spins, proving world-matrix composition through World::GetWorldMatrix() actually works, not just that a parent field exists. That same last entity also carries a "material" block (post-Editor-E8 material assets, renderer/MaterialData.h) -- assets/m_demo_red.material.json's actual, committed GUID (see that file's own .meta sidecar) -- so it renders bright red through ForwardLitColorPipeline instead of ForwardLitPipeline's debug normal-color visualization, proving a material-tinted entity actually looks different, not just that the field round-trips. The final entity references assets/m7_quad.gltf's mesh instead of the shared m1_cube.glb (deliberately, not an oversight: m1_cube.glb predates TEXCOORD_0 -- see cmake/CookAssets.cmake's own comment -- so every one of its vertices samples a texture at UV (0,0), which would just look like one flat color rather than proving anything) and assets/m_demo_checker_tint.material.json ("ForwardLitTexturedColor" shader) -- a live example of the Texture property type, actually showing M7's own checker pattern (not just a solid sampled color) through the RHITexture/descriptor-set plumbing this feature added to the Editor executables, tinted light blue.
